run.question:
Alertmanager alert PrometheusNotConnectedToAlertmanagers (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus since 2026-11-15T04:38:07Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The alert is firing because the Prometheus instance prometheus/prometheus-prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus-0 has no Alertmanager to be connected to: no Alertmanager workload, Service, Endpoints object or volume exists in any namespace of this cluster, although the monitoring.coreos.com Alertmanager CRDs and a working kube-prometheus-stack operator are installed. The rule that fires, as loaded in the Prometheus rule files, is max_over_time(prometheus_notifications_alertmanagers_discovered{job="prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus",namespace="prometheus"}[5m]) < 1 with for: 10m, so a continuously zero discovered-Alertmanager count produces exactly this alert. Prometheus itself is healthy (pod Running/Ready, both containers 0 restarts), and the operator is actively reconciling (the rule-files ConfigMap was refreshed at 2026-11-15T04:31:13Z). The Prometheus pod was (re)created at 04:37:35Z and became Ready at 04:37:51Z, 16 s before the alert's start; no events or container logs are available to explain that recreation, and I could not read the generated Prometheus configuration (Secret) or the prometheus_notifications_* self-metrics, so whether the alerting section is absent or points at non-existent endpoints remains unverified. Either way the discovered count is zero because no Alertmanager exists to discover.

claims.text: The loaded Prometheus rule file (ConfigMap prometheus-prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus-rulefiles-0, key prometheus-prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus-ac4fa589-688e-4d06-9c48-89982b78688c.yaml) defines alert PrometheusNotConnectedToAlertmanagers with expression max_over_time(prometheus_notifications_alertmanagers_discovered{job="prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus",namespace="prometheus"}[5m]) < 1 and for: 10m.

A cluster-wide listing of all 66 pods in all namespaces contains no Alertmanager pod; the Prometheus pod present is prometheus/prometheus-prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus-0 with IP 100.96.5.74 (the instance in the alert), running with 0 restarts.

The cluster's only StatefulSets are chi-clickhouse-main-0-0, jaeger-traces-recorder, prometheus-alert-recorder, topology-monitor, opensearch-cluster-master and prometheus-prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus; there is no Alertmanager StatefulSet (the object the prometheus-operator would create for an Alertmanager resource).

A cluster-wide listing of all 36 Deployments contains no Alertmanager Deployment; in namespace prometheus only prometheus-kube-prometheus-operator (prometheus-operator:v0.85.0) and prometheus-kube-state-metrics exist, both created 2026-11-14T05:24:06Z.

No Service in the cluster (52 Services processed, all namespaces) has a name matching "alert"; the 5 Services in namespace prometheus are prometheus-kube-prometheus-operator, prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus, prometheus-kube-state-metrics, prometheus-operated and prometheus-prometheus-node-exporter, i.e. there is no prometheus-kube-prometheus-alertmanager or alertmanager-operated Service.
No Endpoints object in the cluster (52 processed) has a name matching "alert", so no alertmanager endpoint set exists that Prometheus could discover via service discovery.

The 10 PersistentVolumeClaims in the cluster contain none in namespace prometheus and none named for an Alertmanager; the only alert-related claim is data-recorders/prometheus-alert-records-prometheus-alert-recorder-0 (a data-recorder, Bound 2026-11-15T04:45:27Z).
The 4 Ingresses in the cluster target clickhouse-clickhouse, topology-monitor-svc, jaeger-collector and prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus; none exposes an Alertmanager UI/API.

The Alertmanager CRDs are installed (alertmanagers.monitoring.coreos.com and alertmanagerconfigs.monitoring.coreos.com, created 2026-11-14T05:23:54Z), so the chart/operator could manage an Alertmanager in this cluster but the API objects show none was instantiated as a workload.

The Prometheus StatefulSet prometheus-prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus was created 2026-11-14T05:24:07Z, has replicas 1 and is owned by the custom resource Prometheus/prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus, i.e. the Prometheus CR exists and is reconciled while no Alertmanager resource's workload does.

The Prometheus pod prometheus-prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus-0 has startTime 2026-11-15T04:37:35Z, became Ready at 04:37:51Z, and its containers prometheus and config-reloader are both running with restartCount 0; its storage is inside the pod (no PVC in namespace prometheus), with args --config.file=/etc/prometheus/config_out/prometheus.env.yaml and --storage.tsdb.path=/prometheus.

The Prometheus rule-files ConfigMap prometheus-prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus-rulefiles-0 was (re)created at 2026-11-15T04:31:13Z and already contains the otel-demo alerting and workload-recording rule files, showing the prometheus-operator was reconciling rule content shortly before the alert started.

A cluster-wide event search matching "alert"/"alertmanager" returned only scheduling, volume-provisioning and start events for data-recorders/prometheus-alert-recorder-0 between 2026-11-15T04:45:27Z and 05:18:13Z; no event mentions an Alertmanager object being created, scaled or deleted.

Primary cause: no Alertmanager is deployed for this kube-prometheus-stack, so prometheus_notifications_alertmanagers_discovered for job="prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus"/namespace="prometheus" stays at 0 and the rule (max_over_time<1, for: 10m) keeps PrometheusNotConnectedToAlertmanagers firing. Consistent with the absence of any Alertmanager workload, Service, Endpoints, PVC and Ingress, together with the presence of the Alertmanager CRDs and a reconciling operator.

Alternative, unresolved variant of the same immediate effect: the generated Prometheus configuration may contain an alerting.alertmanagers section that points at a non-existent endpoint (e.g. the operator-generated prometheus-kube-prometheus-alertmanager Service) instead of having no alerting section at all. Both variants yield a discovered-Alertmanager count of 0, and the config Secret prometheus-prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus could not be read to distinguish them.

Consequence (not directly observed): while no Alertmanager endpoint exists, Prometheus cannot deliver notifications for the alerts it evaluates, including those defined by the loaded otel-demo alerting rules (e.g. otel-demo-otel-demo-alerting-rules). Notification counters (prometheus_notifications_* / alertmanager_notifications_*) are not present in the accessible Prometheus view, so this is unverified.

Prometheus itself is not the failing component: the pod prometheus-prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus-0 is Running and Ready with both containers at restartCount 0, and its owning StatefulSet has 1/1 replicas, so the alert is about connectivity to a missing dependency, not about Prometheus availability.

The prometheus-operator is not obviously broken: its Deployment is 1/1 Ready, and the rule-files ConfigMap was regenerated at 2026-11-15T04:31:13Z with the current otel-demo PrometheusRule content, which argues against 'operator failed to create the Alertmanager StatefulSet' and for 'no Alertmanager resource / alerting deliberately not enabled'.

Rejected: an Alertmanager exists but is down, scaled to 0, or unreachable at the network level. There is no Alertmanager pod, StatefulSet, Deployment, Service, Endpoints object or PVC anywhere in the cluster, so nothing of that kind exists to be unreachable; the failure is the absence of the endpoint, not the health of one.

Rejected as the cause: the recreation of the Prometheus pod at 2026-11-15T04:37:35Z. Restarting Prometheus cannot bring the discovered-Alertmanager count below 1 by itself; with an Alertmanager Service present the metric would return to 1 after the first scrape. The cluster contains no Alertmanager object to discover, so the restart is at most a coincidence in time, not the reason for the alert.

Deploy Alertmanager for this stack (kube-prometheus-stack alertmanager enabled, i.e. an Alertmanager resource prometheus-kube-prometheus-alertmanager with its Service) so that Prometheus's alerting.alertmanagers resolves to a real endpoint; if alerting is intentionally absent here, silence or disable the PrometheusNotConnectedToAlertmanagers rule instead, since it will fire permanently in that configuration.

gaps: The metric that drives the alert, prometheus_notifications_alertmanagers_discovered{job="prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus",namespace="prometheus"}, is not readable in the accessible Prometheus view: an exact instant query at 2026-11-15T04:38:07Z and max_over_time(...[5m]) both returned no_data, and {__name__=~"prometheus_notifications.*"} returned no series. The view only exposes job values kube-state-metrics, kubelet, otel-collector and namespace otel-demo, so Prometheus self-metrics appear to be excluded; the metric's zero value is therefore inferred from the firing rule, not read directly.

The generated Prometheus configuration lives in the Secret prometheus-prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus (loaded from /etc/prometheus/config_out/prometheus.env.yaml); secrets cannot be read, so I could not verify whether the alerting section is absent or references a non-existent Alertmanager endpoint, nor which alertmanager namespace/name the operator would target.

Alertmanager custom resources (alertmanagers.monitoring.coreos.com) cannot be listed with the available Kubernetes tools (the kind is not in the supported list), so whether an Alertmanager resource exists with replicas 0, or does not exist at all, is unverified.

Container logs were unavailable for every pod read: prometheus-prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus-0 (init-config-reloader, prometheus, config-reloader), prometheus-kube-prometheus-operator-57d68989cc-hkbnh and data-recorders/prometheus-alert-recorder-0 all returned 0 lines (bytes_read 0) for the window, so operator reconciliation errors and Prometheus 'error sending alerts'/alertmanager-connection messages could not be inspected.

No events exist for namespace prometheus inside the authorized window (query returned no_data), so why prometheus-prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus-0 was recreated at 2026-11-15T04:37:35Z (rollout, eviction or reschedule) is unknown, and no SuccessfulCreate/SuccessfulDelete evidence for an Alertmanager was retrievable.

The timing of the alert relative to the rule is unexplained: with for: 10m the rule should need ~10 minutes of condition, yet the alert's start (2026-11-15T04:38:07Z) is only 16 s after the recreated Prometheus pod became Ready (04:37:51Z). Because the pod has no PVC (emptyDir storage) alert for-state could not be preserved across that restart; I could not verify how the for-duration was satisfied.

The change_history integration is not available in this run, so no deployment/Helm-value change can be confirmed for the 04:29-04:37Z period (namespace otel-demo created 04:29:18Z, rule-files ConfigMap 04:31:13Z, Prometheus pod 04:37:35Z); whether an Alertmanager was ever installed and then removed cannot be determined from the current object state.

The alert reached an Alertmanager that is not a pod or Service in this cluster (no Alertmanager object exists anywhere here), so the identity/location of the Alertmanager that evaluated and sent this notification is unknown and was not visible to the available integrations.
next_steps: Inspect the kube-prometheus-stack release values (e.g. alertmanager.enabled, alertmanager.replicas) and the Prometheus resource spec.alerting / spec.alertmanagerConfigSelector to confirm alerting is intentionally disabled versus misconfigured, using cluster access that can read monitoring.coreos.com resources and the prometheus-operated configuration Secret.

If alerting is wanted, enable the Alertmanager resource and verify that the Service prometheus-kube-prometheus-alertmanager (port http-web/9093) exists with ready endpoints, then confirm prometheus_notifications_alertmanagers_discovered returns 1 for job="prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus".

Check why prometheus-prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus-0 was recreated at 2026-11-15T04:37:35Z (kubelet/node events, operator reconciliation history) and consider persistent storage instead of emptyDir so alert for-state survives restarts.
Confirm with the platform owners which Alertmanager instance produced this notification, since no Alertmanager runs in this cluster.

Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). <none> means the path reached no value in that object, not that the field is absent from the kind; a filtered table is not a full picture of the kind.
